note: Compact treatment: these three services are leaf business services with an identical structural shape — one EE surface, one DI dependency (their own datastore), one AC container, and NO outbound calls (no CE/SE points exist; verified by grep across each module's src/main for RestTemplate/WebClient/FeignClient — none found). Full per-mechanism detail follows the same schema as api-gateway-audit.json; abbreviated here to avoid repeating near-identical evidence three times.

EE-1.mechanisms: none found (no rate limiter, no bulkhead)

DI-1.note: BOUNDARY FINDING: db/mysql/schema.sql exists in-repo, but no application-mysql.yml datasource block and no database service in docker-compose.yml were found. The docker-compose deployment topology implies the active production datasource is externalized to the config-server's backing configuration repository, which is NOT part of this codebase and therefore out of this audit's boundary. What IS verifiable in-repo (test/default profile) is an embedded HSQLDB with no replication, no explicit pool config, no explicit timeout.
DI-1.mechanisms: no replication, no fallback, no explicit timeout, no explicit pool found in-repo

AC-1.mechanisms: actuator dependency present but unwired (no docker-compose healthcheck for this service — verified by absence in docker-compose.yml, contrast with config-server/discovery-server which have one); no graceful shutdown config; memory limit only (512M), no CPU limit, no reservations; no startup probe

DI-1.note: Same boundary finding as customers-service — production datasource likely externalized to config-server backing repo, out of boundary; in-repo evidence shows embedded HSQLDB with no replication/pool/timeout declared.
DI-1.mechanisms: no replication, no fallback, no explicit timeout, no explicit pool found in-repo

AC-1.mechanisms: same pattern as customers-service: actuator present, unwired; no graceful shutdown; memory-limit-only resource declaration; no startup probe

DI-1.note: Same boundary finding as the other two leaf services.
DI-1.mechanisms: no replication, no fallback, no explicit timeout, no explicit pool found in-repo

AC-1.mechanisms: same pattern; additionally uses spring.cache (cache-names: vets, application.yml) as an in-process read-through cache in front of vet lookups

quality.set_aside_detail: In-process read-through cache (CacheConfig.java, vets.cache.ttl=10 in application.yml) reduces load on the DI dependency but has no slot in the current MS-1.1 profile — the profile's DI protections (replication/fallback/timeout/pool) model protection of a call to the store, not application-level caching in front of it. Logged as a genuine profile coverage gap, not scored.
